blocks.text: Job 20 is part of the sustained debate that follows Job’s lament. Zophar, like the other friends, treats suffering as evidence of wrongdoing and describes the wicked person’s ruin; Job rejects that diagnosis of his own suffering. The friends’ earlier seven days of silent presence contrast sharply with the harm their later rigid explanations cause.

Later reflection on Job’s steadfastness can refer to his persistence through suffering and to the story’s outcome. It should not be taken to require silent endurance of abuse or to prevent seeking escape and protection.
